graph.summary: alteplase → Plasminogen → Fibrinolysis → Thromboembolism → Pulmonary embolism

evidence.snippet: Tissue plasminogen activator (t-PA) is a serine protease that binds to fibrin-plasminogen complex, catalyzing the conversion of plasminogen to plasmin
evidence.explanation: Alteplase is the recombinant t-PA product (rt-PA, Activase) reviewed here; t-PA catalyzes conversion of plasminogen to active plasmin.

evidence.snippet: the main function of tPA released from the endothelium is to convert fibrin-bound plasminogen into active plasmin, thus dissolving the fibrin meshwork of blood clots
evidence.explanation: Alteplase is recombinant human tPA; tPA converts fibrin-bound plasminogen into active plasmin.

evidence.snippet: convert plasminogen into plasmin to initiate fiber lysis
evidence.explanation: Plasmin, generated from plasminogen, initiates fiber (fibrin) lysis, i.e. it drives fibrinolysis.

evidence.snippet: a proenzyme, plasminogen, which can be converted to the active enzyme plasmin, which will degrade fibrin
evidence.explanation: Active plasmin derived from plasminogen degrades fibrin, the proteolytic core of fibrinolysis.

evidence.snippet: This illustrated review focuses on fibrinolysis-the degradation of blood clots or thrombi
evidence.explanation: Fibrinolysis is the degradation of blood clots/thrombi, i.e. the process itself disrupts the thromboembolus.

evidence.snippet: thrombus that detaches and lodges in the pulmonary circulation being a cause of APE
evidence.explanation: A thrombus that detaches and lodges in the pulmonary circulation (a thromboembolus) is the cause of acute pulmonary embolism (APE).
